chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Muhammad ibn Hammam, who said: He narrated to us Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik, who said: He narrated to me Muhammad ibn Shihab from Abdullah ibn Yunus al-Subi'i, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"I love for every believer to wear five rings: with ruby, which is the most splendid of them; with agate, which is the purest of them for God and for us; with turquoise, which is the delight of the gaze of the believers (men and women); and with Chinese iron, which I love to wear and do not dislike wearing when meeting the people of evil, to extinguish their evil. I love to have it made, for it scatters the unruly from jinn and humans, and what God reveals with the white stones, the two Ghariyyan."

I said: O my master, what is the virtue in it? He said: "Whoever wears it and looks at it, God writes for him, for every glance, a visitation (reward) whose reward is the reward of the prophets and the righteous. And if it were not for God's mercy upon our Shiah, the separation (or distinctiveness) from it would reach a degree that cannot be found for a price. But God has made it easy for them so that their rich and their poor may wear it."

key_terms.زَوْرَة: visitation or a specific measure of reward
key_terms.يَتَخَتَّمَ: to wear a ring on the little finger

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rings for believers according to Imam al-Sadiq and what are their virtues?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the virtues of five specific rings, emphasizing that the 'Ghariyy' stone is particularly cherished for its ability to repel the mischief of jinn and humans, serving as a spiritual shield. He notes that gazing upon this stone grants the reward of the prophets and righteous ones, highlighting God's mercy in making it accessible to both the rich and the poor, thus ensuring its benefits are not limited by wealth. This tradition reflects the Shia emphasis on tangible spiritual aids (al-zawahir al-mubarakah) that connect the believer to divine grace and protection.
